p: The beauty of Clip 'n Climb is that you don't need to be fit, strong or experienced to have a great time. The walls cover a wide range of difficulties, so beginners can build up confidence on the easier ones before tackling the tougher challenges. The auto-belay means you can let go whenever you like, and you'll be lowered gently back down, which takes away much of the fear for first-timers.

A few tips for your session. Take short breaks to rest your arms, keep a drink to hand, and don't feel you need to finish every wall. It's about fun, not records. Encourage each other from the ground, as a bit of cheering goes a long way when someone's nervous. Spectators can usually watch the action too, so grandparents can come along and enjoy it without climbing.

Gloucester has more to offer than many people realise. The National Waterways Museum Gloucester, in a historic warehouse at the docks, tells the story of Britain's canals and offers boat trips in the warmer months. Rugby fans can catch Gloucester Rugby at Kingsholm, a famously atmospheric ground. If you want to burn off even more energy, Robinswood Hill Country Park on the edge of the city has woodland trails and views over the Severn Vale. For a bigger adventure, the Forest of Dean is a short drive west, with miles of walking and cycling routes.
